transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose what brings me in is... this memorial I'm putting together for my brother. It's just gotten a lot bigger than I originally meant it to. 

I've been spending most of my days chasing down specific songs, calling folks up, and planning out these displays and trips for it. My wife is the one who really pushed for this appointment, to be honest. She says I’ve pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I usually do because I'm so focused on getting this done.
Beyond being focused on this project, how has your overall mood been lately—would you say you've felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or perhaps more irritable than your usual self?

Well, I guess it's a bit of both. Mostly I just feel... lit up, I suppose. Really full of purpose. It feels like the whole town is finally going to understand our family once this is all done. 

But then... yeah, I have been more irritable, too. If my wife or someone over at the senior center tries to slow me down, or if they start questioning how I'm doing the display... I just snap at them. I don't necessarily mean to, I just don't have the patience for anyone getting in the way of it right now.
Have you felt like you are receiving any special messages or have you been seeing or hearing things that others around you don't seem to notice?

Well, no special messages, I don't think. But as for hearing things... yes, actually. 

Sometimes when I’m sitting at the kitchen table sorting through his old song sheets, I hear my brother’s voice. It's clear as day. He'll just be humming right behind me, or sometimes he even tells me which tune should come next for the display. My wife is usually right there in the house and she doesn't hear a thing, but I know what I'm hearing.
Looking back over the last few years, have there been any significant periods where you felt deeply low, hopeless, or lost interest in almost all of your usual activities?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, but nothing like what you're describing. I haven't felt deeply low or hopeless. 

Up until I started this memorial project, I was always pretty steady with my routine—you know, keeping up with the yard and my walking group. I can't really think of a time in the last few years where I just stopped caring about my usual activities or felt lost like that.

Are you only hearing your brother's voice during this recent period where you've been feeling so 'lit up' and focused on the memorial, or have you experienced these voices at other times in your life when you were feeling like your usual self?

No, it's only been lately. Before I got so swept up in this memorial work—right after my brother passed—I never heard his voice in the house. I never felt like the songs were telling me what to do or anything like that. All of that just... started up at the same time as this burst of energy and all the nonstop planning for the display. When I was feeling like my usual self, I never experienced anything like this.
